candidate_sources.title: Mycosphaerella coffeicola (brown eye spot of coffee) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: Small brown spots occur on the leaves, more obvious on the upper surface. The spots can grow up to 15 mm diameter; they have light brown or sometimes light grey centres, surrounded by a wide, dark brown ring, and a yellow margin. Cultural control includes spacing, N and K nutrition, shade (35-65%), and prune to improve air movement. Chemical control includes copper (protectant) and triazoles (systemic). Mycosphaerella coffeicola (asexual form: Cercospora coffeicola) is the causal pathogen.

candidate_sources.title: Cercospora Leaf Spot and Berry Blotch of Coffee
candidate_sources.snippet: Circular brown spots with bright grey centres and yellow haloes are typical of brown-eye leaf spot caused by Cercospora coffeicola. The disease causes lesions on leaves as necrotic spots, defoliation, fruit injuries, reduced productivity, and lower beverage quality. The highest disease pressure occurs when temperature is 20–28°C and continuous environmental wetness lasts 36–72 hours. Cultural control includes arranging seedlings for good air movement and providing adequate nitrogen and potassium nutrition.

candidate_sources.title: Fact sheet - Coffee brown-eye spot (142) - Lucid Apps
candidate_sources.snippet: Brown eye spot causes small brown spots on coffee leaves, mostly 5-10 mm, with bright grey centres and yellow haloes. Spores form in the grey centres. Brown irregular to oval spots also occur on the berries, which may ripen prematurely and develop off-flavors during processing. The disease is favored when coffee plants suffer from poor nutrition or insufficient shade. In severe cases, can cause leaf fall of seedlings and stem dieback in nurseries.

candidate_sources.title: Hemileia vastatrix (coffee leaf rust) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet covering Identity, Overview, Distribution, Dispersal, Hosts/Species Affected, Diagnosis, Biology & Ecology, Seedborne Aspects, Natural Enemies, Impacts, Prevention/Control. Symptoms include small yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces that expand into larger round spots with bright orange to red pustules on undersurface. Pathogen: Hemileia vastatrix (multicellular basidiomycete fungus, order Pucciniales). Management includes cultural control (tree spacing 3x3m, weed removal, pruning), chemical control (copper oxychloride), and genetic resistance (Catimor hybrids).

candidate_sources.title: Coffee Rust | Plant Disease, Description, Symptoms, & Control | APS Net
candidate_sources.snippet: APS educational resource describing coffee rust (CLR) caused by Hemileia vastatrix. Symptoms: small, pale yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces; as spots expand, masses of orange urediniospores appear on undersurfaces; leaves develop bright orange to red spots, finally brown with yellow border; rust pustules are powdery and orange-yellow on underleaf surface. Disease significance: one of the most economically important diseases of coffee worldwide; can cause yield losses up to 35%; epidemic in Central America/Caribbean (2011) damaged 70% of farms in Latin America with >$3 billion in losses by 2021.

candidate_sources.title: Hemileia vastatrix Berkeley & Broome - Purdue CAPS Extension Factsheet
candidate_sources.snippet: Purdue Crop & Pest Specialists (CAPS) extension factsheet on Hemileia vastatrix, the causal agent of coffee leaf rust. Provides comprehensive information on the pathogen, identification, distribution, hosts affected, and management strategies for coffee leaf rust in extension format.
